description: A garden entry vignette photographed at dusk at low-to-seated camera height with a normal lens, off-center composition placing the garden column slightly left of center. A substantial square tapered pillar of rough-hewn speckled gray-beige granite sits at the edge of a smooth pale stone paver terrace. Behind and around the pillar, a lush mixed garden planting creates rich textural layering — clusters of gray-green and burgundy echeveria succulents fill the foreground ground level, while deeper in the bed tall ornamental grasses with feathery plumes sway above burgundy Japanese maple foliage. Russet-toned shrubs with autumn coloring fill the middle distance. The exterior wall of the building in the background is clad in large-format travertine-hued stone panels with a matte finish, warm and architectural. A glazed exterior column or architectural detail at the right edge adds depth. The landscape is captured in the blue hour, the ambient sky having faded to a deep charcoal-indigo, throwing the garden plantings into silhouette except where caught by warm amber light. A glowing warm amber light emanates from within a translucent post-cap element at the top of the granite column, casting a soft pool of honeyed illumination across the top of the stone and spilling warm light onto the surrounding garden and terrace paving. The palette is warm amber against deep charcoal blue, with russet and sage garden tones.
